CSP Summary.System Description: Vyond is the only all-in-one video creation platform built for business and government organizations. With a focus on privacy and security, simplicity of use, and powerful video creation, Vyond for Government grants federal and public sector agencies access to our flagship platform, enabling transformation of critical information into engaging videos for employees, partners, and constituents - effectively and at scale.

01.desc: Configure ALL information resources to limit inbound and outbound traffic
01.note: V4G uses AWS Security Group to limit the traffic. Check the AWS Trusted Advisor Security Groups – Specific Ports Unrestricted and Security Groups – Unrestricted Access, V4G meets most qualifications

02.desc: Design systems to minimize the attack surface and minimize lateral movement if compromised
02.note: Inventory all EC2 hosts to guarantee all hosts are segmented by VPC to minimize lateral movement if compromised

03.desc: Use logical networking and related capabilities to enforce traffic flow controls
03.note: Confirm all hosts are attached to at least 1 security group to guarantee the traffic flow is enforced by the cloud native network

04.desc: Use immutable infrastructure with strictly defined functionality and privileges by default
04.note: V4G utilizes Terraform Infrastructure as Code (IaC) to manage infrastructure and Packer to build immutable AWS AMIs. Each application runs on a dedicated instance profile with the principle of least privilege. GitHub Actions are used to implement Blue/Green deployments through CI/CD pipelines, ensuring consistent and controlled rollout.

05.note: V4G benefits from AWS Shield Standard, which provides automatic protection against common DDoS attacks at the network and transport layers. The architecture follows AWS best practices for DDoS resiliency, including using Amazon CloudFront, Route 53, and WAF to provide additional layers of protection. These measures help to ensure high availability and mitigate denial-of-service threats effectively.

06.desc: Design systems for high availability and rapid recovery
06.note: Check the AWS Trusted Advisor Fault Tolerance Checks, V4G meets most qualifications

07.desc: Ensure cloud-native information resources are implemented based on host provider’s best practices and documented guidance
07.note: V4G hosts on AWS and follows AWS Well-Architected Framework to do the implementation.

01.desc: Harden and review network and system configurations
01.note: V4G hardens the configuration based on CIS benchmark and monthly reviews the configuration with Tenable. All failed items have been completed the deviation request process and all warning items have been completed the review and are in the process of the deviation request

02.desc: Encrypt or otherwise secure network traffic
02.note: V4G has encrypted the network traffic of Application Load Balancers, RDS Aurora, Elasticache Redis.

03.desc: Encrypt all federal and sensitive information at rest
03.note: V4G has encrypted data in S3 buckets, RDS Aurora, Elasticache Redis, the image files and all backup database snapshots.

04.note:
V4G centrally manages infrastructure and application configurations using a combination of tools and AWS services:
1. Packer: used to build immutable and standardized AWS AMI
2.Terraform: used to consistently provision infrastructure and enforce configuration baselines.
3.AWS SSM Parameter: used to centrally store and retrieve parameters at runtime.
4. AWS Config: is enabled to continuously monitor and record configuration changes.

05.desc: Enforce system and information resource integrity through cryptographic means
05.note: V4G has encrypted all AWS EBS to store the image

06.desc: Use automated key management systems to manage, protect, and regularly rotate digital keys and certificates
06.note: V4G uses AWS Key Management Service to manage and automatically rotate the key

07.desc: Use a consistent, risk-informed approach for applying security patches
07.note: V4G has subscribed to notifications for AWS Linux 2023 update to inform V4G for applying security patches, and uses a Security Tracker to guarantee the deployment is controlled

01.desc: Enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) using methods that are difficult to intercept or impersonate (phishing-resistant MFA) for all user authentication
01.note: V4G has enforced YubiKey 5 FIPS Series (CMVP #3914) to be the MFA device of AWS and Google Identity (the other external service must SSO with Google Identity) to guarantee phishing-resistent MFA

02.desc: Use secure passwordless methods for user authentication and authorization when feasible, otherwise enforce strong passwords with MFA
02.note: V4G has enforced strong passwords for users, and the other external service must SSO with Google Identity

03.desc: Enforce appropriately secure authentication methods for non-user accounts and services
03.note: V4G does not allow the non-user accounts/services to do the console login

04.desc: Use a least-privileged, role and attribute-based, and just-in-time security authorization model for all user and non-user accounts and services
04.note: V4G follows the Separation of Duties Matrix to fulfill the requirement

05.note:
V4G follows AWS document to implement the Zero Trust Design principle and the following are implemented:
1. Strong Authentication (refer to KSI-IAM-2)
2. Least Privileges Access (refer to KSI-IAM-4)
3. Micro Segmentation (refer to KSI-CNA-2)
4. Full Encryption (refer to KSI-SVC-2, KSI-SVC-3)
5. Endpoint Security
6. Logging and Alert Automated Policy Enforcement(refer to KSI-MLA-1)

06.desc: Automatically disable or otherwise secure accounts with privileged access in response to suspicious activity
06.note: V4G hosts on AWS and adopts Google Workspace to be the document repository, the automation management is inherited from the security control of each side. Moreover, V4G has adopted Wazuh and AWS CloudWatch to detect the abnormal account behaviors

01.desc: Operate a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) or similar system(s) for centralized, tamper-resistent logging of events, activities, and changes
01.note: V4G adopts Wazuh as the SIEM, collecting data from Google Workspace and AWS to detect abnormal activities

02.note: Wazuh helps to review and analyze the log immediately and V4G runs the investigation for the suspicious behaviors when they occur

03.desc: Rapidly detect and remediate or mitigate vulnerabilities
03.note: V4G remediates the vulnerability based on 30 (High) - 90 (Moderate) - 180 (Low) days principle and track the progress in the monthly ConMon Report

04.desc: Perform authenticated vulnerability scanning on information resources
04.note: V4G runs the installed agent to run the authenticated vulnerability scanning with Tenable (FR#: FR1814276801), the installed agent runs credentialed checks to guarantee the authenticated vulnerability scanning

05.desc: Perform Infrastructure as Code and configuration evaluation and testing
05.note: V4G adopts Terraform as the IaC and monthly runs the configuration scanning with Tenable (FR#: FR1814276801)

06.desc: Centrally track and prioritize the mitigation and/or remediation of identified vulnerabilities
06.note: V4G follows FedRAMP requirements and adopts the POA&M sheet to centrally track and prioritize the remediation of identified vulnerabilities

01.note: V4G adopts on-premise Trend Micro Deep Security to monitor system modifications

02.desc: Execute changes though redeployment of version controlled immutable resources rather than direct modification wherever possible
02.note: V4G adopts Blue-Green Deployment strategy and all hosts are immutable and relaunched with the new version of the image per monthly deployment

03.desc: Implement automated testing and validation of changes prior to deployment
03.note: V4G has executed the automation process to test and verify the change per deployment

04.desc: Have a documented change management procedure
04.note: V4G has followed FedRAMP requirements to document the change management procedure, all change requirements must follow the procedure

05.desc: Evaluate the risk and potential impact of any change
05.note: V4G has evaluated the risk and potential impact of each change

01.desc: Have an up-to-date information resource inventory or code defining all deployed assets, software, and services
01.note: V4G runs the asset inventory for each deployment and modification

02.desc: Have policies outlining the security objectives of all information resources
02.note: V4G has outlined the security objective as the commitment in the policy

03.note: The vulnerability disclosure program is maintained and published in the help center

04.desc: Build security considerations into the Software Development Lifecycle and align with CISA Secure By Design principles
04.note: The SDLC is documented and the security function is covered in the Technical Specification phase to guarantee Secure by Design

05.desc: Document methods used to evaluate information resource implementations
05.note: The method to run the automation testing plan for the implementation is documented

06.desc: Have a dedicated staff and budget for security with executive support, commensurate with the size, complexity, scope, and risk of the service offering
06.note: The dedicated staff and budget for security is arranged. However, for the confidential purpose there is no evidence can be published

07.desc: Document risk management decisions for software supply chain security
07.note: V4G has documented the Supply Chain Risk Management Plan and follows the plan to perform the decision

01.note: V4G has identified all third-party vendors and place the inventory information in the SSP, see the section 6 and 7 of the evidence file

02.desc: Regularly confirm that services handling federal information or are likely to impact the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of federal information are FedRAMP authorized and securely configured
02.note: V4G annually reviews all external services are FedRAMP authorized and securely configured

03.desc: Identify and prioritize mitigation of potential supply chain risks
03.note: V4G has identified the potential supply chain risks and reviewed it annually

04.desc: Monitor third party software information resources for upstream vulnerabilities, with contractual notification requirements or active monitoring services
04.note: V4G has subscribed to the third party vendor's subscription for the status notification

01.desc: Ensure all employees receive security awareness training
01.note: V4G has performed and ensured all participants receive and complete the security awareness training with KnowBe4 (FR#: FR2201340492)

02.desc: Require role-specific training for high risk roles, including at least roles with privileged access
02.note: V4G has requested the participants to complete the security awareness training based on the role

01.desc: Define Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPO)
01.note: The RTO is 8 hours and the RPO is 24 hours, based on the data backup frequency

02.desc: Develop and maintain a recovery plan that aligns with the defined recovery objectives
02.note: V4G has developed a recovery plan that aligns with the defined recovery objectives, and reviews the plan annually

03.desc: Perform system backups aligned with recovery objectives
03.note: V4G has backup the required images and data to align with the RTO and RPO

04.desc: Regularly test the capability to recover from incidents and contingencies
04.note: V4G tests the contingency plan annually

01.desc: Report incidents according to FedRAMP requirements and cloud service provider policies
01.note: V4G has followed federal requirements and documented the Incident Response Plan

02.desc: Maintain a log of incidents and periodically review past incidents for patterns or vulnerabilities
02.note: V4G has reviewed the incident annually for patterns or vulnerabilities and built the scenario for IR/DR drills

03.desc: Generate after action reports and regularly incorporate lessons learned into operations
03.note: V4G has documented the lessons learned session in the Incident Response Plan
